title: Hybrid prober for prefill and decode kernel policies
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Problem: Kernel selection at runtime currently uses coarse heuristics that do not adapt fast enough to mixed workloads and heterogeneous GPU fleets. We observe 8-18% latency regressions versus optimal kernel combos for short prefill-heavy requests and decode-heavy chat sessions. Goal: Build a low-overhead hybrid prober that (1) runs extremely lightweight micro-benchmarks during safe windows (cold-start, warmup, or sampled requests) to estimate short-prefill and short-decode path cost for a specific model + hw combination, (2) aggregates sequence-length percentiles and per-model prefill/decode ratio to drive an online policy, and (3) surfaces a robust fallback and rollout strategy to preserve p95/p99 latency SLOs and tail-cost targets.
background: Current runtime picks kernel variants primarily from static profiles keyed by model family and a small set of sequence lengths. With newer attention implementations (flash-attn v2, cutlass fused kernels, Triton custom kernels) and quantization variants, the optimal kernel changes based on (a) token distribution (prefill length and decode burst size), (b) GPU architecture (A100, H100, RTX series), and (c) KV-cache behavior. We need a real-time, low-regret selector that learns quickly without high probe overhead.
proposed_solution: Design a hybrid prober that combines (A) a prefill microprobe: run a 4-8 token artificial prefill pass using model-specific warmup context to measure prefill kernels' effective throughput and memory pressure; (B) a decode microprobe: simulate 2-6 decode steps to measure per-token latency for candidate decode kernels; (C) a lightweight online learner: a contextual Thompson-sampling bandit that uses features {model_id, hw_family, seq_len_percentile_bucket, quantization_profile, recent_probe_scores} to pick kernels; (D) short time-window smoothing and decay to avoid thrashing; (E) rollout policies with canary slices and automatic rollback on SLO breach. Probe execution windows are restricted to: cold instance startup, first N requests after model load, and 0.5% of sampled live requests (configurable). Probe cost capped at <2% of total tokens served for a model across a 24h window.
metrics_and_targets: Success metrics: 1) end-to-end p95 token latency improvement >= 6% vs baseline on mixed workloads; 2) 99th percentile decode latency does not regress >2% during rollout; 3) probe overhead <= 2% of tokens/day per model; 4) successful kernel selection accuracy (chooses within 5% of empirical best) >= 85% on held-out traces.
acceptance_criteria: Hybrid prober implemented behind a runtime feature flag (configurable per-tenant)
Microprobes implemented for both prefill and decode with <1ms scheduling overhead per probe
Bandit learner evaluated on replay traces with documented uplift >= targets
Canary rollout mechanism integrated with Console metrics (canary % control) and automatic rollback triggers for latency or error increase
Design doc and microbenchmark harness published (Drive link) and test coverage for prober code paths >= 80%

comments: 2025-02-18 - Maya Rodriguez: Created ticket and initial proposal after perf review. Attached A/B baseline traces showing candidate regressions. Requesting ETA from Perf Eng.

2025-02-20 - Ethan Park: Started a lightweight prefill harness prototype — using 6-token synthetic prefill we can distinguish flash-attn vs cutlass in ~4ms median difference on H100. Need to validate memory-pressure behavior on multi-tenant Dedicated nodes.

2025-02-24 - Priya Sharma: Implemented decode probe sketch and a scheduler hook to place probes during low-CPU windows. Noticing occasional probe interference when running during large batches; limiting probes to instance-level load < 40% reduces interference.

2025-02-27 - Anil Gupta: Bandit learner initial model: contextual Beta-Bernoulli with per-arm priors seeded from offline microbenchmarks. Replay on week-long traces gives ~72% immediate-opt picks, improving to ~88% after 1h of online decay smoothing. Will add time-decay hyperparameter.
2025-02-28 - QA (J. Lee): Test plan reviewed. Edge case: very short-lived instances where probes can't complete — will add a fallback to static profile and mark instance as non-probable for 12h.

2025-03-01 - Product (R. Nguyen): Confirmed customer-facing constraints: disable probes for privacy-sensitive tenants by default and surface probe cost in billing dashboard. PM supports rollout to Hosted first, then Dedicated after SRE sign-off.
notes: Rollout plan: Hosted API -> 1% canary for 48h -> 5% for 72h -> full. Dedicated customers opt-in via console. If p99 latency increases by >3% or error rate increases by >0.2pp during canary, automatic rollback and incident alerting to oncall. Future work: extend probe to memory/temperature-aware placement and multi-model colocations.
